today.h: The AI Trade's Reprieve: a Chip Bounce Lifts the Nasdaq 1.1% — With Only Three Sectors Green
today.c1: The AI trade got a reprieve. The Nasdaq rose 1.11% to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 0.41% to 7,690.73; the Dow slipped 36.38 points (0.07%) to 51,966.03. Chips snapped their longest slide since 2008 — SOXX +1.7%, SMH +1.6% — with WDC +6.1%, SNDK +5.5%, STX +3.4%, MU +3.0%, MRVL +4.1%, AMD +1.8%, INTC +2.4% and NVDA +1.4%. Amazon added 5.0% on Morgan Stanley's top-pick call; Tesla 3.8% before Wednesday's results. But breadth was thin: only three of 11 sector ETFs closed green, utilities -2.0% and real estate -1.2% as the 10Y rose 6bp to 5.15% and French protests lifted yields across Europe; the euro slipped 0.2%, the dollar rose to 102.0. Oil split by contract: Brent settled $109.55 (-0.3%) after ranging $107-$110 on Trump's Russia waiver, while WTI's expiring November contract settled $103.66 (+2.2%) and December $98.54 (-0.5%). Gold -0.5% to $4,160.7; bitcoin +0.4% to ~$81.9k; VIX -7.8% to 18.44.
today.c4:
• The AI trade's tell is breadth, not the index: a 1.1% Nasdaq day with three sectors green is a repair, not a rotation — watch whether chips hold their gains past Wednesday's Meta and Tesla prints.
  • The rate file is the binding constraint: the 10Y at 5.15% (+6bp) charged utilities (-2.0%) and REITs (-1.2%) on a day tech rose — a clean test of which side of the book can pay for duration.
  • The barrel is a contract story as much as a war story: WTI's November settle at $103.66 (+2.2%) versus December's $98.54 (-0.5%) is expiry mechanics — don't read the front-month pop as a fresh escalation.
  • Next gates: Meta and Tesla on Wednesday, then the FOMC on Oct 27-28 — with October odds ~16%, the market's base case is a hold; December ~92% is where the risk lives.

chains.t: ① The AI Trade's Reprieve: Chips Snap the Longest Slide Since 2008
steps: The setup: last week the Nasdaq fell 4.5% — its worst week since June — and the S&P 2%; chipmakers logged their longest losing streak since 2008, with SOXX down 4% on Friday alone

The turn: dip buyers met the open — the VanEck Semiconductor ETF climbed nearly 3% by midday, on pace to end a nine-day losing streak (CNBC) — as investors bet the AI investment boom still supports earnings
The leadership: memory and semis led — WDC +6.1%, SNDK +5.5%, STX +3.4%, MU +3.0%, MRVL +4.1%, AMD +1.8%, INTC +2.4%, NVDA +1.4%
The fade: SOXX closed +1.7% after trading +3.7% early; SMH +1.6% after +3% midday; CoreWeave went from +7% to -0.4% — the bid thinned into the close
The scoreboard: Nasdaq +1.11% to 26,430.89, S&P +0.41% to 7,690.73, Dow -0.07% to 51,966.03, Russell 2000 +0.25% — a tech repair, not a broad rally
chains.d: The reprieve: a nine-session chip slide met dip buyers — enough to lift the Nasdaq 1.1%, not enough to broaden the tape.

news.fact: Another burst of selling in technology shares drove the Nasdaq 100 to its worst week since the April 2025 tariff turmoil as investors questioned the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade. Chipmakers fell for an eighth straight day, the longest slide since 2008. CoreWeave Inc., a cloud-computing services provider whose bonds recently hit levels that typically signal distress, sank 12%. The S&P 500 lost 1.1%.

The S&P 500 rose 0.4%, coming off its worst week since June, and the Nasdaq composite rallied 1.1% because it's full of technology stocks. The majority of U.S. stocks outside of AI and tech fell, though, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average swung between losses and gains before finishing with a drop of 36 points, or 0.1%.

A rebound in chipmakers buoyed the stock market as dip buyers emerged on bets the artificial-intelligence investment boom will continue to support solid earnings. Following a rout in one of the most-crowded bets, a gauge of chip giants climbed 1.6%. The Nasdaq 100 added 1.2%.

AI-tied stocks were among the biggest risers Monday. Roundhill's Memory ETF (DRAM) rebounded 4% following a nearly 6% decline Friday, with components Western Digital, Sandisk, Micron Technology and Seagate Technology advancing up to roughly 6%. The broader iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed up almost 2% after a 4% drop to end last week, with component Intel rising 2.5% in part because of a rating upgrade from JPMorgan. Nvidia rose nearly 1.5%.

Chip stocks rallied Monday, on pace to end a nine-day losing streak. In midday trading, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) climbed nearly 3%, fresh off nine consecutive losing days, as traders flocked back to the tech space and took a risk-on posture. Nvidia gained about 2% and Advanced Micro Devices added 3%; Marvell also added nearly 7%.
The S&P 500 opened at 7,702.77, traded as high as 7,731.18 and closed at 7,690.73; the Nasdaq Composite's session high was 26,613.15 against a 26,430.89 close.

chains.t: ② The Narrow Tape: a 5.15% 10Y, a French Shock — and Three Sectors Green
steps: The rate leg: the 10Y rose 6bp to 5.15% and the 30Y 5bp to 5.48% — the move came even as the Nasdaq rallied
The French source: weekend protests drove European indexes more than 1% lower, lifted French yields and pushed the euro down 0.2%; the dollar rose 0.2% to 102.0
The domestic bill: utilities -2.0%, real estate -1.2%, financials -0.8% and staples -0.5% — the rate-sensitive cohorts paid for the 10Y; Ameriprise fell 4% on a BofA downgrade
The breadth: only three of 11 sector ETFs closed green — ConsDisc +1.8%, Tech +1.4%, Materials +0.1% — and the majority of stocks outside AI and tech fell (AP)
The tell: the VIX fell 7.8% to 18.44, so this was rotation, not de-risking — the fear gauge never confirmed the narrow breadth
chains.d: The split: AI paid for itself while rates taxed everything else — three sectors green, the Dow flat, and a VIX that said no one was panicking.

news.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5.30% earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002.

In Europe, the losses were sharper, and indexes slid more than 1% following violent protests that could ultimately force the French government to increase its spending to ease voters' anger. That in turn could put even more pressure on bond markets, and yields cranked higher worldwide.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the value of the greenback against a basket of foreign currencies, was up 0.2% at 102.00, aided by the dollar's 0.2% rise against the euro, which is slipping amid nationwide French protests about the cost of living.

Ameriprise Financial tumbled almost 4% after Bank of America slashed its rating on the stock to underperform. The iShares Mortgage Real Estate Capped ETF (REM) hit a low of $16.71, its lowest level since April 6, 2020; it was last down more than 3% on the day and has fallen more than 24% this year.
The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.15%, up from 5.09% at the prior close, according to the Treasury's daily yield curve; the 30-year closed at 5.48% from 5.43%.

chains.t: ③ The Barrel's Two Prices: a Russia Waiver, a Hormuz Threat — and an Expiry Squeeze
steps: The waiver: Trump's Friday order paused Graham Act sanctions and tariffs on Russia for up to 60 days, tied to a diesel deal expected to move ~2.3M barrels this month and up to ~7.6M a month — Brent fell 2.1% to $107.57 early

The chokepoint: Iran said it has 'no choice' but to assert control over Hormuz — after a weekend in which two tankers were reported hit in the Persian Gulf and Houthis targeted Yanbu — Brent reversed through the session
The settles: Brent December -0.3% to $109.55 after ranging $107-$110; WTI November +2.2% to $103.66 into Tuesday's expiry; December WTI -0.5% to $98.54 — a $5.12 backwardation

The physical check: Dated Brent ~$117, down almost $16 in a week; Gulf flows ~80% of pre-conflict levels (Energy Secretary Chris Wright); Iraq exporting 3.4M bpd — supply is loosening under the headlines
The positioning cap: CTAs were at 100% maximum long in both benchmarks (Kpler) and Friday's rally left Brent overbought on the 9-day RSI — there were no fresh buyers left for the squeeze
chains.d: The barrel: a waiver pulled the bid, a chokepoint returned it, and expiry did the rest — Brent flat-ish, WTI's front month squeezed, and the physical market quietly loosening.

news.fact: President Donald Trump waived key sanctions and tariffs under the Graham Act, raising expectations of additional Russian fuel exports. Trump's October 16 executive order waived specified Graham Act sanctions and tariffs, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio outlined a review lasting up to 60 days.

Brent crude futures fell $2.29, or 2.08%, to $107.57 per barrel by 0619 GMT on Monday, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures dropped $1.95, or 1.92%, to $99.46. The planned Russian exports were expected to begin at approximately 2.3 million barrels this month before potentially increasing to around 7.6 million barrels per month, Reuters reported.

Oil fluctuated near a five-month high. Prices briefly gained this session, before easing, after Iran said it has 'no choice' but to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz, while US lawmakers continue to resist President Donald Trump's diesel export deal with Russia. WTI for November delivery gained 2.2% to settle at $103.66 a barrel; November futures expire the next session. The more-active December contract was down 0.5% to settle at $98.54. Brent for December settlement fell 0.3% to settle at $109.55.

The Dated Brent benchmark, which underpins prices in Europe, traded near $117 on Monday, down almost $16 from a week prior. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News that Persian Gulf oil flows had recovered to about 80% of their pre-conflict level, although refined-product shipments remain constrained. Iraq has exported more than 3.4 million barrels a day of crude so far this month, according to the country's oil minister.

Trend-following commodity trading advisers are sitting at 100% maximum long in both Brent and WTI, suggesting they've exhausted buying capacity for now, according to Kpler. The prior session's leg higher sent prices into overbought territory on the 9-day Relative Strength Index.

Over the weekend, a Saudi helicopter crashed near the border with Yemen and Houthi rebels targeted Yanbu, a crucial export hub, while UK maritime operations said two tankers reported being hit in the Persian Gulf.

chains.t: ④ The Cushion: Upgrades, a 29% Earnings Runway — and a Fed on Hold
steps: The broker turn: Goldman put CoreWeave on its buy list with a $106 target (~73% above Friday's close); JPMorgan lifted Intel to neutral; Morgan Stanley named Amazon a top pick at $350
The strategist: Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson told clients the pullback is nearing an end — 'be ready' for either a rapid reconciliation or a slower bleed into November
The earnings runway: more than 70 S&P 500 companies report this week and Q3 blended growth is tracking 29% (FactSet); Meta and Tesla report Wednesday
The global stabilizer: Kospi +1.8% after -14.5% last week; bitcoin +0.4% to ~$81.9k after topping $83k intraday; gold -0.5%
The Fed: October hike odds ~16%, December ~92% — Warsh's silence is still read as a hold into the Oct 27-28 meeting
chains.d: The cushion: upgrades, a 29% earnings runway and a Fed on hold gave the dip buyers cover — the floor holds as long as the earnings week does.

news.fact: Goldman Sachs upgraded CoreWeave to buy from neutral, noting that '[next 12 months] datapoints on contract economics are likely to be more positive than the market expects.' The firm also dialed back a price target to $106 from $139, calling for nearly 73% upside from the prior close.

Investors should prepare to add risk to their portfolios as a months-long pullback in parts of the equity market nears an end, according to Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson. 'We advise investors to be ready for either a very rapid reconciliation or a slower bleed into November because in our view, that will be the time to add risk rather than shun it,' Wilson wrote.

Amazon jumped 5% to lead Dow Jones Industrial Average gainers Monday after Morgan Stanley analysts called the Magnificent Seven tech giant a 'Top Pick' and lifted their price target on the stock to $350 from $335.
Analysts are forecasting overall growth of 29% for companies in the S&P 500 from the prior summer, according to FactSet.
More than 70 S&P 500 companies are due to report this week, including Magnificent Seven members Tesla Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc.
In stock markets abroad, rebounds for AI stocks helped South Korea's Kospi jump 1.8% to recover some of its 14.5% drop from last week.
According to the CME's FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in a 16 per cent chance of a rate hike this month and a 92 per cent chance of an increase in December.

mtd.h: October, Thirteen Sessions In: a Record, Three Repricings — and a Round Trip
mtd.d: S&P 7,651.5 → 7,690.73 (+0.51% MTD): one record close, a 5.36% yield spike, three repricings and a chip repair — the index is level, the leadership is not.
mtd.c1: Thirteen sessions into October and the S&P is +0.51% at 7,690.73 — still 1.6% below the 7,818.93 record set on 10/6 — while the Nasdaq is -1.60% and the Dow +2.08%. The month's arc: an S&P record close in the first week, then three repricings (wireless on 10/9, the AI complex on 10/12-13, the CPI-PPI pair on 10/14-15), and a chip-led repair that stopped the slide. The 10Y touched a 24-year high of 5.36% on 10/7 and closed at 5.15% (-14bp MTD); October hike odds went from 22% before CPI to a 37% peak and back to ~16%. Beneath the index: Energy +10.2% leads, Tech -5.0% lags — a ~15-point spread — and eight of 11 sectors are positive. Oil: WTI +14.6% (Nov), Brent +11.8% (Dec). Gates: FOMC Oct 27-28, PCE Oct 29.
mtd.c4:
• October's shape is a round trip, not a trend: the S&P is +0.51% MTD but 1.6% below its 10/6 record — the month's gains were made in the first week and defended since.
  • The dispersion trade still pays: Energy +10.2% vs Tech -5.0% is a ~15-point spread — own the barrel's beneficiaries, rent the AI complex until its funding costs stop rising.
  • The month's last gate is the PCE print on Oct 29, two days after the Fed: October odds ~16% price a hold, so the risk is December (~92%) — watch the 10Y at 5.15% through both.

chains.t: ① October's Round Trip: a Record, Three Repricings — and a Chip Repair
steps: The high: the S&P closed at 7,818.93 on 10/6 — its first close above 7,800 and the month's only record; the Nasdaq's own record run ended the next session
The first repricing: wireless on 10/9, when the telecom majors fell on SpaceX competition
The second: the AI complex on 10/12-13 — memory, equipment and neocloud names led the selling
The third: the CPI-PPI pair on 10/14-15 pushed October hike odds from 22% to a 37% peak before they round-tripped to ~16%
The sum: +0.51% MTD, still 1.6% under the record — a round trip, not a new leg
chains.d: October so far: one record, three repricings, one repair — the index is level, the leadership is not.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close; the Dow remains just over 5% shy of its Aug. 5 record.
Shares of the country's largest telecommunications giants are slumping amid worries about growing competition from SpaceX.

Memory makers Micron and SK Hynix saw their stocks fall after Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies announced significant progress on a new memory-cell design aimed at increasing storage density.

According to CME FedWatch, traders now see a 37% likelihood the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting in two weeks, up from 22% before the reading, and a 91% likelihood the central bank will lift rates at least a quarter-percentage point at its December meeting.
Chip stocks rallied Monday, on pace to end a nine-day losing streak. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained 3.7% and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) rose 3.2%.

chains.t: ② The Month's Split: Energy +10.2%, Tech -5.0%
steps: Sector map: Energy +10.2%, Staples +8.2%, ConsDisc +5.2%, Utilities +4.9% — eight of 11 sectors are positive for the month
The gap: the best-to-worst spread is ~15 points — Energy +10.2% against Tech -5.0%
The index math: Dow +2.08% vs Nasdaq -1.60% — the old-economy index beat the AI-heavy one by 3.7 points
Inside tech: Tech is still -5.0% MTD — the month's damage is not repaired
The message: money rotated, it did not leave — eight sectors green, the S&P positive, the Nasdaq still down
chains.d: October's split: the barrel and the defensives got paid; the AI complex paid the rent — a rotation, not an exit.

news.fact: Slightly more than half of the stocks in the S&P 500 fell, but all but seven of the 75 stocks in the index's tech sector closed lower. Among the biggest decliners were chip companies, reflecting mounting worries about how long the frenzy over the AI buildout will last.
The majority of U.S. stocks outside of AI and tech fell, though, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average swung between losses and gains before finishing with a drop of 36 points, or 0.1%.

An outperformance of the so-called quality factor and a decline in the equal-weighted version of the S&P 500 are set to come to an end, providing an opportune window to snap up stocks, Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson said.

chains.t: ③ The Barrel, Thirteen Sessions In: $98 to $110 and Back
steps: The path: Brent's December contract began October near $98, crossed $100 on 10/1, held a $100-107 corridor for two weeks, then touched $110 on 10/16
The drivers: Hormuz attack counts, a Russian refinery strike and the diesel deal kept re-arming the premium
The offsets: the IEA's release, a 17M-barrel SPR offer and the 10/16 Russia waiver
The scoreboard: Brent $109.55 (+11.8% MTD) near a five-month high; WTI $103.66 (+14.6%), its best since September
The shape: every dip was bought, but the highs stopped rising after 10/16 — a war premium that policy could dent, not break
chains.d: October's barrel: war kept re-arming the premium, policy kept capping it — a $100-110 month with no resolution.

news.fact: Front Month ICE Brent Crude for Dec. delivery gained $2.47 per barrel, or 2.42% to $104.72 this week — up for two consecutive sessions.

Brent crude futures settled $3.94, or 3.7%, higher at $109.86, the highest since May 19, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures closed $3.44, or 3.5%, higher at $101.41, the highest since September 17.
'Constraints on the diesel market will extend well into next year,' the International Energy Agency warned, with gasoil supply falling short of demand in 4Q26.
On Friday, the U.S. offered up to 17 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the Department of Energy said.
Brent for December settlement fell 0.3% to settle at $109.55 a barrel. WTI for November delivery gained 2.2% to settle at $103.66; the more-active December contract was down 0.5% to settle at $98.54.

qtd.h: Q4's Opening Ledger: +0.51%, a Record, a 24-Year Yield Top — and Four Gates Still Ahead
qtd.d: From 9/30's 7,651.5 to 7,690.73 (+0.51% QTD): the quarter has banked one record and one yield spike — and none of its big gates yet.
qtd.c1: Q4 is thirteen sessions old and the S&P is +0.51% (7,690.73), the Nasdaq -1.60%, the Dow +2.08%. The opening ledger: an all-time closing high of 7,818.93 on 10/6; a 24-year intraday high of 5.36% on the 10Y on 10/7, now 5.15% (-14bp QTD); three repricings — telecom, the AI complex and the inflation prints — all booked inside the quarter's first two weeks; Brent +11.8% and WTI +14.6%. What has not happened: the FOMC (Oct 27-28), the PCE print (Oct 29), the bulk of Q3 earnings (Meta and Tesla Wednesday) and the Nov 3 midterms. The quarter's test is whether +0.51% survives those four gates.
qtd.c4:
• Q4's ledger is thin: +0.51% for the S&P, -1.60% for the Nasdaq — the quarter has banked a record and three repricings, not a direction.
  • The quarter's remaining gates are all in the next two weeks: FOMC (Oct 27-28), PCE (Oct 29), Meta/Tesla (Wednesday), midterms (Nov 3) — position for the gates, not the tape.
  • The rate bill is the swing: a 10Y above 5% keeps leadership narrow; a break back below 5% would let the AI complex's repair broaden.

chains.t: ① What Q4 Has Banked — and What It Hasn't
steps: Banked: 7,818.93 on 10/6 — the S&P's only record close of the quarter so far — and a 5.36% print on the 10Y on 10/7, the highest in 24 years
Banked: a full round trip in October hike odds — 22% before CPI, a 37% peak, ~16% now — and a 10Y that ends at 5.15% (-14bp QTD)
Not yet: a Fed decision — the FOMC meets Oct 27-28 with October odds ~16% and December ~92%
Not yet: the earnings verdict — Q3 growth is tracking 29%, but Meta and Tesla report Wednesday and the chip complex reports alongside them
The ledger: S&P +0.51%, Nasdaq -1.60%, Dow +2.08% — the quarter has paid the barrel and the defensives, not the AI complex
chains.d: Q4's first thirteen sessions banked a record and a yield spike — the verdict still sits with the Fed and the earnings week.

news.fact: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close.
The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.15%, up from 5.09% at the prior close; the 30-year closed at 5.48% from 5.43%, according to the Treasury's daily yield curve.
Analysts are forecasting overall growth of 29% for companies in the S&P 500 from the prior summer, according to FactSet.

chains.t: ② The Quarter's Rate Bill: 5.15% and a 24-Year High
steps: The 10Y opened Q4 at 5.29%; it printed 5.36% on 10/7 and closed at 5.15% — a net -14bp, but still above 5%
The path was violent: a 5.36% peak, a 5.09% trough last week and 5.15% now — after October hike odds round-tripped from 22% before CPI to a 37% peak to ~16%
The cost: mortgage REITs sit at their lowest since April 2020 — the clearest read on what a 5% long end does to leveraged carry
The offset: Q3 earnings are tracking 29% growth while the 10Y sits above 5% — the equity case now rests on earnings outrunning the long end
The gate: the Oct 27-28 FOMC — December odds ~92% say one more hike this year, just not this month
chains.d: The quarter's rate bill: a 10Y that touched 5.36% and still sits above 5% — the bull's tax, and the reason leadership is narrow.

news.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield topped 5.30% earlier this month and touched its highest level since 2002.
The iShares Mortgage Real Estate Capped ETF (REM) hit a low of $16.71, its lowest level since April 6, 2020; it has fallen more than 24% this year.
According to the CME's FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in a 16 per cent chance of a rate hike this month and a 92 per cent chance of an increase in December.

chains.t: ③ The Quarter's Four Gates: FOMC, PCE, Earnings, Midterms
steps: Oct 27-28: the FOMC — October odds ~16%, December ~92%; Warsh's silence has been read as a hold
Oct 29: the PCE print — the inflation series the Fed watches, the day after the meeting
This week: Meta and Tesla on Wednesday, with Lam Research and Texas Instruments — the AI trade's proving ground
Nov 3: the midterms — energy prices and the Russia diesel deal are campaign issues
The rest of Q4: whether +0.51% becomes a base or a peak
chains.d: Q4's next gates — FOMC, PCE, megacap earnings, midterms — decide whether +0.51% is a base or a peak.

news.fact: The Federal Reserve's communications blackout period runs from Oct 17 through Oct 29, ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting, according to the Atlanta Fed's 2026 blackout calendar.

Results are due from Netflix and SpaceX after the closing bell on 10/20, followed on 10/21 by Meta Platforms and Tesla, which will kick off Magnificent 7 reports for the latest quarter. IBM's numbers are also due.
Trump's decision came not long after he said earlier this month he had reached a diesel deal with Russia in an attempt to bring down elevated U.S. fuel prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

ytd.h: The Bull at +12.35%: AI Earnings Carry, a 99bp Rate Bill
ytd.d: S&P +12.35%, Nasdaq +13.72%, Dow +8.12% with thirteen Q4 sessions logged — AI capex and 29% earnings growth carry; a 10Y up 99bp, an 80% barrel and a hot CPI-PPI pair tax the rest.
ytd.c1: The year's base case still holds: AI capex and earnings carry the S&P to +12.35% (7,690.73) and the Nasdaq to +13.72%, with the Dow +8.12%; the bull turned four on 10/12. Against it: a 10Y at 5.15% (+99bp YTD, with a 24-year high of 5.36% printed on 10/7), Brent +80.0% and WTI +80.5% as the war grinds through an eighth month, and a hot September CPI (3.7%) and PPI (6.3%). Beneath the index: Energy +51.6% leads the year, Tech +29.2%, Health +13.5%; Comms -6.5% and ConsDisc -4.2% lag, Utilities -3.1%. Gold -4.2%, bitcoin -6.4%, the dollar +3.8%; December hike odds ~92%.
ytd.c4:
• The year's engine is intact: AI capex and 29% earnings growth have carried the S&P +12.35% through a 99bp rise in the 10Y — earnings are doing the work rates used to do.
  • The credit file is the newest risk: CoreWeave's 15% bond yield and Anthropic's valuation reset are the market's stress gauges — watch them before the AI complex.
  • The year's last macro gate is December (~92% hike odds): a pause in October is priced; the December decision is where the bull's 2027 setup gets set.

steps: The engines: AI capex — hyperscalers are heading toward $1 trillion a year — and earnings, with Q3 growth tracking 29%
The scoreboard: S&P +12.35%, Nasdaq +13.72%, Dow +8.12% — the AI-heavy index still leads despite October's repricing
The referee: the 10Y at 5.15%, +99bp YTD, and a 24-year high of 5.36% printed on 10/7
The taxes: WTI +80.5% and Brent +80.0% as the war grinds on; September CPI 3.7% and PPI 6.3%
The breadth: Energy +51.6% leads; Comms -6.5%, ConsDisc -4.2% and Utilities -3.1% lag
chains.d: The year's base case: AI and earnings compound, rates and oil tax — a four-year bull still faster than its referee.

news.fact: Chipmakers, which have soared over 80% so far this year, were clear underperformers on the day, falling 3.4%.

The bull market turned four on Monday, with many strategists expecting more room for stocks to run. However, concerns over an AI bubble, elevated Treasury yields, and geopolitical uncertainty present hurdles.

The S&P 500 rose 31.29 points to 7,690.73, the Dow dipped 36.38 to 51,966.03 and the Nasdaq rallied 290.85 to 26,430.89. Analysts are forecasting overall growth of 29% for S&P 500 companies, according to FactSet.

chains.t: ② The Rate and Inflation Tax
steps: The long end: the 10Y from 4.16% to 5.15% (+99bp); the 30Y from 4.84% to 5.48% (+64bp)
The Fed: a September hike, its first since July 2023 — with December odds ~92%
The prints: September CPI 3.7% y/y and PPI 6.3% y/y; October hike odds round-tripped 22% → 37% → ~16%
The cross-asset echo: the dollar +3.8%, gold -4.2% — real rates, not war, set the tone for both
chains.d: 2026's tax: a 99bp rise in the 10Y and a second inflation wave — the September hike was the year's regime change.

news.fact: Tight global crude supplies during the Iran war have sent US crude soaring more than 60% so far this year, stoking inflation pressures. In response to those pressures, the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates in September for the first time since July 2023.
Consumers pay $4.33 a gallon for gasoline, compared to about $3.08 per gallon a year earlier, according to AAA.

According to CME FedWatch, traders now see a 37% likelihood the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting in two weeks, up from 22% before the reading, and a 91% likelihood the central bank will lift rates at least a quarter-percentage point at its December meeting.

chains.t: ③ The AI Platform's Credit Test
steps: The buildout moved onto credit: CoreWeave carries $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans; a June bond at 9.625% yielded 15% at last week's peak
The scare: Anthropic IPO investors weighed a ~$1.5T valuation, down from ~$2T; OpenAI's revenue was reported ~$50 billion, not ~$70 billion
The repair: a sell-side upgrade this week has not reversed the move — the stock is -25% over the past week
The test: Meta and Tesla report Wednesday; Lam and Texas Instruments this week — capex guidance is the number that matters
chains.d: The AI platform's year: capex compounding on credit — October's stress test was a financing scare; the earnings week is the answer.

news.fact: Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%.

A little over a week after it was reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue was approaching $70 billion, the AI lab is said to have told investors the real figure is some $20 billion lower — 'approaching $50 billion.'

Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, with some discussing a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion previously expected.
CoreWeave shares went from a 7% morning gain to a 0.4% loss, following a 25.2% slide last week.

CAL.note: A light macro week: no CPI, payrolls or FOMC decision, and the Fed is in its blackout (Oct 17–29), so no Fed speakers.
